body:
CONTEXT. PR #442 (commit 2f3c160) added the manifest entries to @adlc/init's ADLC_GITIGNORE_LINES so a scaffolded repo can commit its C11 evidence ledger. That fix is real but reaches ONE of four hand-maintained copies of the same ordered contract. The other three are unchanged, so the ticket's stated bug persists on every path that does not go through @adlc/init:

1. packages/core/lib/scaffold-hygiene.mjs GITIGNORE_STANZA — this is the stanza the HARNESS scaffolders use. plugins/adlc-cursor/lib/scaffold.mjs, plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/scaffold.mjs and plugins/adlc-pi/lib/commands.mjs all call @adlc/core's ensureGitignore. Any repo scaffolded through cursor, opencode or pi therefore still keeps its evidence ledger local-only, and `gate-manifest enable` refuses it outright on the two-sided gitignore contract. This is the single largest remaining gap.
2. packages/tickets/lib/migrate.mjs GITIGNORE_STANZA (used by migrationGitignoreText) — carries '!.adlc/manifest.jsonl' but none of the manifest.d entries, so a repo that runs the legacy-store migration comes out with its root ledger tracked but forest mode unusable.
3. packages/gate-manifest/lib/enable.mjs MARKER_NEGATION_LINES — the lines `enable` PRINTS as the remediation when it refuses. It omits '.adlc/manifest.d/*.tmp-*', so an operator who follows the printed advice lands in a state the scaffolders would then change.

This repository's own .gitignore is also missing '.adlc/manifest.d/*.tmp-*', so it would track gate-manifest enable's crash residue (.store.json.tmp-<hex>), which lands in discoverSegments().invalid — a set both recoverOpenSegment and gate-manifest adopt refuse on.

A nine-round adversarial-review loop against a branch that attempted all of this at once (local ref t-init-gitignore-refactor, tip 301af5d, NOT pushed) confirmed each defect below by execution rather than inference. That branch is reference material only: it grew to +1039 lines across four packages and its last four review rounds each found a defect introduced by the previous round's fix, which is why the work is being re-scoped into this ticket rather than landed as one change. Whoever picks this up should treat the findings as the specification and re-derive the implementation in reviewable slices, not cherry-pick that branch wholesale.

DEFECTS CONFIRMED (each was reproduced, not inferred):

A. Sibling copies missing the contract — items 1-3 above, plus this repo's own .gitignore.

B. Ordering is not repaired, only membership checked. Effectiveness in gitignore is POSITIONAL (last match wins). A stanza negation sitting above the `.adlc/*` anchor, or above a LATER duplicate anchor, is dead; treating 'present anywhere' as satisfied leaves it dead forever while the run reports success, and every subsequent run then reports 'unchanged' — the tool cannot repair the state it helped create. @adlc/core handles some of this; @adlc/init and @adlc/tickets do not. Reproduced with two fixtures: negations above the anchor, and a trailing second anchor.

C. Re-ignore placement. The checkout-local entries ('.lineage', '*.lock', '*.tmp-*') must outrank EVERY negation, including ones the user wrote themselves. @adlc/tickets' insertion walk skips past any /^!?\.adlc\// line — re-ignores included — so a missing negation splices BELOW an existing '.lineage' and revives it as trackable, the exact harm the stanza exists to prevent.

D. Whole-directory and alternate anchor spellings. '.adlc/' and '.adlc' EXCLUDE the directory, and git cannot re-include anything inside an excluded directory, so the entire stanza below is dead while the write reports success — @adlc/core has no normalization for this (@adlc/init does). Exact-string anchor matching also misses '/.adlc/*', '.adlc/**', '/.adlc/**' and an anchor with trailing whitespace; each unrecognized spelling sends the scaffolder down the append path that drops a fresh blanket ignore BELOW the user's own negations.

E. CRLF. @adlc/core splits on '\n' alone, so every line of a CRLF .gitignore keeps its '\r' and '.adlc/*\r' never matches the anchor: the file reads as anchorless, a second anchor is appended below the user's negations, and last-match-wins kills them. @adlc/init already splits /\r?\n/.

F. Symlinked .gitignore is read THROUGH. @adlc/core does readFileSync on the path, which follows a symlink; the target's bytes become the file content and are rewritten verbatim into the real file the function then creates. Reproduced: with '.gitignore -> /tmp/outside/secrets.txt' containing SECRET_TOKEN=..., the repo's real .gitignore afterwards began with that line. @adlc/init already refuses via rejectSymlinkComponents, so the copies diverge on a SECURITY property. Note the fix must not simply throw: aborting takes every other scaffolding step down with it, and a 'skipped' result is worse than useless unless callers actually surface it (the three plugin scaffolders return the result object without inspecting it).

G. Structural reasoning never checks its own output. Each of B-F is a different gitignore shape the grammar checks missed; a user-authored '.adlc/manifest.d/**' below the block is another (not a stanza line, not an anchor spelling, does not start with '!'). The durable fix is to ask git the same two-sided question `gate-manifest enable` asks — after writing, and before reporting 'unchanged' — so the scaffolders and the activation command cannot certify and refuse the same repository.

H. Widening enable's PROBE list is a breaking change. `gate-manifest enable` runs as an idempotent health check on the already-enabled path. Adding '*.tmp-*' to the required-ignored probes flips every repository activated under the older advice from exit-0 already-enabled to exit-2 refuse-ignored on upgrade, on a perfectly healthy ledger. Blocking (.lineage, locks — actively harmful) must stay a refusal everywhere; residue should be advisory on the already-enabled path and enforced on greenfield, where the repo is being set up correctly from the start. Refusal messages must name the exact path probed, or the new mode is undiagnosable.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
AC1 — parity: a test binds all four copies (init's constant, core's stanza, tickets' migration stanza, gate-manifest's printed advice) plus this repository's own .gitignore, asserting the manifest entries and their relative order match. Verify: node --test packages/init/test/gitignore-parity.test.mjs.
AC2 — harness scaffolders: a repo scaffolded through @adlc/core's ensureGitignore can commit .adlc/manifest.jsonl, .adlc/manifest.d/, the activation marker and a segment filename, while .lineage, *.lock and *.tmp-* stay ignored. Verify: behavioral test using real `git check-ignore` in a temp git repo.
AC3 — ordering repair: fixtures covering a negation stranded above the anchor, a duplicate trailing anchor, a pre-existing re-ignore whose negations are missing, and a present-but-dead re-ignore each end with the two-sided contract holding. Verify: behavioral tests in the init, core and tickets suites.
AC4 — anchor recognition: whole-directory ignores, '/.adlc/*', '.adlc/**', '/.adlc/**' and an anchor with trailing whitespace are all recognized, and a user-authored '.adlc/' negation below the block still works afterwards. Verify: table-driven tests whose spelling list is DERIVED from the source set, so a spelling added is covered and one dropped fails.
AC5 — CRLF: a CRLF .gitignore is parsed, gains no second anchor, and the user's own negations survive. Verify: test.
AC6 — symlink: a symlinked .gitignore is refused without reading through it; the target is untouched AND its contents never appear inside the repository; the refusal does not abort the rest of the scaffold; the plugin scaffolders surface the refusal rather than reporting success. Verify: test asserting the target file is byte-identical and no real .gitignore holding its contents was created.
AC7 — output verification: a repo whose own rule outranks the ADLC block is never reported 'unchanged'/'updated' as though fine — the scaffolder emits a warning naming the likely cause. Verify: test using a user-authored '.adlc/manifest.d/**'.
AC8 — no breaking upgrade: a repository already in forest mode whose .gitignore satisfies the pre-existing contract but lacks '*.tmp-*' still reports already-enabled (exit 0) with an advisory warning; the same repo missing '.lineage' still REFUSES; greenfield activation enforces the full contract. Verify: three tests over gate-manifest enable.
AC9 — full suite green and mutation-gate clean: npm test; node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12.
AC10 — trust-root prosecution: packages/** is a rails deny-path (tickets T37/T38), so this is trust-root tier — a distinct-provider cross-model approve bound to the reviewed revision is required. Verify: adlc prosecute --base main exits 0.

PROCESS NOTES. (1) Land this in SLICES, not one branch: the reference branch's last four review rounds each found a defect introduced by the previous round's fix, which is the signature of a change that has outgrown one review. A natural first slice is the sibling copies (defect A) alone, since that is the live user-facing gap. (2) Content parity is not behavioral parity — a test that binds the four lists by line content will still certify copies whose ordering logic differs, which is how defect C survived. (3) Do not edit an existing ticket's body in a PR; rails-guard-ci rejects it. (4) The mutation gate rewrites prose inside string literals — reword rather than pin. (5) Run the FULL suite before pushing.
title: The manifest gitignore contract reaches only @adlc/init: three sibling copies still leave scaffolded repos unable to commit evidence
